deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes compare two structures on a finite family I of pseudolines in the real projective plane, assumed to have no bigons (digons).
- The 2-dimensional arrangement is the cell decomposition of RP^2.
- The '1-dimensional arrangement' (ens. 1-dim.) is the combinatorial 1-skeleton: vertices, edges, and which pseudoline carries which vertices in which (unoriented, cyclic) order.

Goal. Pages 51-54 prove that the functor from the groupoid of 2-dim arrangements without bigons to 1-dim arrangements is fully faithful (stated as a theorem on the next page). The tool is to recover the 2-dimensional structure locally, triangle by triangle.

Triangle orientation. For a triple J of pseudolines forming a triangle K_J with vertices a_i (i in J), one picks for each vertex a supplementary pseudoline D_{a_i} in I\J through a_i. Together with J this gives a 6-line configuration K_{J'}. Its 1-dim combinatorics falls into cases I, II, III. Case I is the generic 'circular order' case, where a_i is opposite a'_{i+1} on D_{a_i}; case II is where a_i is opposite a'_i. These cases determine an orientation of K_J via the 'opposite' points alpha_i on the edges.

Top of this page: conditions (A6), for when the three D_i are not concurrent. One requires (1) that K_{J'} be of type (III) or (II), and (2) that the orientation of K_J so obtained not depend on the choice of J'. These are necessary conditions on a 1-dim structure for it to come from a 2-dim arrangement, and they feed the 'essential image' conditions A1-A5(6).

Remaining degenerate case. Every choice of supplementary pseudolines through the vertices a, b, c is concurrent, so the triangle-orientation test cannot be run. Grothendieck asserts this forces card I = 6. The arrangement is then the complete quadrangle, drawn in the margin:
- four triple points a, b, c, d (d inside triangle abc);
- the six pseudolines joining them pairwise;
- three further double points alpha = ad∩bc, beta = bd∩ca, gamma = cd∩ab, the intersections of 'opposite' lines.

The vertex count is f = 4 + 3 = 7. Check: C(6,2) = 15 = 4·3 + 3. Every line carries exactly 3 vertices, so the 1-dim data are very weak: a cyclic order on 3 points is trivial up to reversal. Hence the 1-dim situation is 'entirely described' by the four triple points and the three extra points. He then begins a standard description of the corresponding 2-dim arrangement, continued on the next page with the labelling a, b, c / alpha, beta, gamma / lambda_a, lambda_b, lambda_c.

In modern terms this arrangement is the simplicial arrangement A(6,1) in Grünbaum's catalogue: 7 vertices, 18 edges, 12 triangular faces (Euler characteristic 1). It is the projectivized braid / Coxeter arrangement of type A_3, with symmetry group S_4. The three diagonal points correspond to the three pairs of opposite edges, i.e. to S_4/V_4 ≅ S_3. This would explain the mention of a Klein four-group V_4 in the parenthesis, if that reading is right.
errors: The implication 'all supplementary triples concurrent ⇒ card I = 6 and the arrangement is the complete quadrangle' is asserted without proof. It needs an argument that every pseudoline outside J passes through a vertex of K_J and that there is exactly one such line per vertex. Plausible, but only sketched.

The page is a draft with heavy cancellations. The text sequence 'arrangement formé des f=4+3 sommets' is duplicated, and the parenthetical '(= groupe de couleurs V_4)' is unclear. No mathematical error is visible beyond the gaps of a working draft.

ideas.what: Recovering the 2-dim cell structure (orientation of each triangle) of a bigon-free pseudoline arrangement from its 1-dim combinatorial data, via auxiliary 6-line subconfigurations; consistency conditions (A6) for the essential image.
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of an (oriented-matroid) arrangement from its cocircuit graph / 1-skeleton; realizability of local sequences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cordovil–Fukuda (1993); Babson–Finschi–Fukuda (2001); related: Björner–Edelman–Ziegler (tope graph determines OM, 1990); Felsner–Weil on local sequences (2001)
ideas.where_published: Pseudoline arrangements appear only in these Montpellier notes as far as I know; unsure about any letter.

ideas.what: Identification of the exceptional configuration where the local test fails: the complete quadrangle with 6 lines, 4 triple points and 3 diagonal double points.
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial arrangement A(6,1) = projectivized A_3 braid/Coxeter arrangement

missed.claim: Grothendieck proves (next page) that the bigon-free 2-dim pseudoline arrangement is determined, functorially (full faithfulness on groupoids), by its 1-dim combinatorial skeleton. This page treats the exceptional case, which is the A_3 braid arrangement. This anticipates the later oriented-matroid literature on reconstructing arrangements from cocircuit graphs, where small non-uniform configurations are precisely the delicate cases. His formulation as full faithfulness of a functor between groupoids, plus an explicit programme to describe the essential image by local axioms, is not how that literature is phrased.
missed.quote: Mais cela implique que card I = 6, et que l'arrangement est l'arrangement formé des f = 4+3 sommets
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, this is an early (c. 1981) independent treatment of 1-skeleton reconstruction for pseudoline arrangements. The 'essential image' programme (characterizing which 1-dim structures come from arrangements) parallels realizability questions for local sequences and cocircuit graphs. It is mainly of historical rather than new-mathematical value.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a case analysis inside a reconstruction proof; the exceptional configuration (complete quadrangle / A(6,1)) is classical. The interest is the context: an early, functorial, unpublished treatment of reconstructing pseudoline arrangements from 1-dim data, predating the oriented-matroid literature on this. The page itself contains no striking new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: '∈ [I \ J]' rather than '∈ [I \]'. The J is partly lost in the struck-out word 'distincts de'.
'Il reste enfin à regarder le cas où' is correct. The marginal insertion reads roughly 'dans le cas où pour chaque D_i ∈ [I∖J] … trois pseudo-droites passent par un point'; it is uncertain.
'que l'arrangement est isomorphe à l'arrangement formé des f = 4+3 sommets (dont 4 triples), et 6 ps. droites' is likely. The phrase '(passant par des triangles)' is probably a misreading.

'les ps. droites qui les relient deux à deux' (joining the four triple points pairwise) is correct. The extra points are 'les trois points d'intersection supplémentaires étant les intersections des ps. droites "opposées"'.

'La situation … 1-dimensionnelle (ensemble combinatoire)' is plausible. The ending 'entièrement décrite par ses triangles' is better read as describing it by its four triple points and the extra points.

'Pour l'une des quatre sommets' is probably 'par l'ens. des quatre sommets triples'. The parenthetical '(= groupe de couleurs V_4)' is very uncertain; it is possibly a reference to the S_4/V_4 symmetry or to an arrangement label.
A marginal figure (not transcribed) shows triangle a, b, c with interior point d and points alpha on bc, beta on ca, gamma on ab: the complete quadrangle.
